runs.prompt: A steep zigzag concrete staircase climbing a hillside residential neighborhood of Seoul at about 2 AM: tightly packed old houses, rooftop green water tanks, tangled power lines, a distant city skyline glowing below. A tired young office worker woman in a long padded coat and office lanyard climbs the stairs, head bowed, face lit cold cyan by the smartphone in her hand. At each of three landings of the staircase (near, middle, far) sits the SAME huge minhwa-style tiger wearing an oversized modern streetwear hoodie, each tiger leaning out and holding out a paw with a grin. The woman's tote bag hangs open with only a few white round Korean rice cakes (tteok) left; each tiger already clutches one white rice cake that glows like a little phone screen. Trail of rice-cake crumbs on the steps. The feeling: she is being robbed one small piece at a time. Original artwork. Contemporary reinterpretation of traditional Korean folk painting (minhwa) — the tiger drawn the old minhwa way (big round comical eyes, toothy mischievous grin, bold ink-outlined stripes, slightly cartoonish proportions) — blended with modern cinematic digital illustration of present-day Seoul. Visible hanji paper texture and soft ink wash. Palette: deep indigo-navy night, saffron-orange tiger, cold cyan smartphone glow, warm sodium streetlight amber. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, numbers, signs with writing, captions, watermarks, logos, brand marks or app interface text anywhere in the image; phone screens show only abstract glowing light. Keep the top 22% of the frame as calm, mostly empty dark night sky (space for a title added later) and the bottom 10% as a simple dark area. Natural hands with five fingers. Not in the style of any specific living artist.

A steep zigzag stairway in an old hillside Seoul neighbourhood at night, seen from slightly below and to the left. Small flat-roofed houses with rooftop water tanks stacked up the hill, a few thin power lines. One tired young office worker in a long padded coat climbs the stairs, head bowed into the glowing phone held in both hands. On three landings going up (big in the foreground right, medium in the middle, small near the top) sits the same grinning minhwa tiger wearing an oversized hoodie, each one holding out a paw palm-up, and each already holding one round white rice cake (tteok). Her open tote bag shows only two rice cakes left; a few rice-cake crumbs on the steps. A big flat full moon sits off-centre in the navy sky. Original illustration made to look like a hand-printed RISOGRAPH poster: only four flat spot inks — fluorescent orange, deep federal-blue/navy, warm mustard yellow and off-black — on cream uncoated paper. Visible coarse halftone dots, slight misregistration between ink layers (1-2 mm offset), uneven ink coverage, paper grain and tiny dust specks. Drawing done with confident brush-and-ink linework like a traditional Korean folk painting (minhwa) woodblock: the tiger has the old minhwa character — big round goggle eyes, wide toothy comical grin, bold blunt stripes, chunky stylised paws — drawn as flat shapes, not realistic fur. People drawn simply with few lines, matte flat color, small simple faces. Composition asymmetric and graphic with generous negative space; strong silhouette readable from far. Leave the top 24% of the frame as flat dark navy ink with only a little texture (title space) and keep the bottom 9% flat navy too. AVOID: glossy highlights, 3D rendering, airbrushed gradients, oversaturated neon, bokeh, lens flare, perfectly symmetrical layout, plastic-looking skin, excessive micro-detail, cluttered backgrounds. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, numbers, signage writing, fake glyphs, watermarks, logos or app interface anywhere; phone screens are plain flat yellow-white light. Hands simple with correct finger count or hidden in pockets/sleeves. Not in the style of any specific artist.
